text:
Claude Giroux is 38 and still the kind of player a coach trusts with the hard minutes. Ottawa uses him about 17 a night in the middle of the lineup, and the Senators take 58% of the expected goals at five on five (the quality of chances) when he's out there, about seven points better than without him.

The points (3 goals, 11 in 19 games) undersell that. Ottawa has scored nearly four fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which is the sort of thing that evens out. His own shooting is right on his expected goals, so this is the real Giroux: more passer than finisher, and a quiet defensive asset. Evolving-Hockey had him 47th of 401 forwards in wins above replacement last season, with opponents' chances shrinking when he's on.

He came into the season with 1,165 career points, 1,000 games of them as a Flyer. Our range for his season: 39 to 60 points.
